content.thinking:
There's a timing mismatch here - the recorded flag toggle event at 11:19:41 comes after the logs already show partial rollout values shifting at 11:14:00, which is before the actual error spike. This implies the official change-log timestamp likely doesn't reflect when the flag actually started propagating; the real transition began earlier than what's officially recorded.

Either way, the correlation is unmistakable: monthly-spend-feature=on triggers the ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py:47, driving the error rate from 0.105 up past 0.345, which is a textbook feature-flag-toggle failure mode since code and config are untouched. I've confirmed no deployments occurred in that window via get_changes, ruling out bad-deployment as the cause, so I'm confident in attributing this to the flag flipping from off to on.

hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was turned on (rolling out between 11:14 and 11:15), and the account-page code path it enables throws a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 on every request that hits it, driving error_rate from baseline (~0.01) up to 0.30-0.35. No deployment or code change landed in this window; only the two flags moved, and reverting the toggle removes the broken code path without redeploying anything.

supporting_evidence.claim: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
monthly-spend-feature=off 140 / on 60 - 200 evaluations ... ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47

monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations ... ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 ... WARN io-shop: account page error rate at 34.50% over the last minute
0.105 at 11:14:00Z rising to 0.345 at 11:15:00Z in the rule_reading/error_rate column, coincident with the flag rollout, while p50/p95/p99 and cpu/memory stay flat

hypotheses.subject: legacy-checkout-fallback
hypotheses.summary: legacy-checkout-fallback was also switched off at the same time; its only visible effect in the logs is the pre-existing, low-rate ClientDisconnected errors (unrelated to the spike), so it does not explain the error-rate jump to 30%+.

supporting_evidence.claim: feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off
legacy-checkout-fallback=off - 200 evaluations ... ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection
